subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What browser handoff trust model and UI ownership should OpenClaw implement for managed-browser login workflows?
rationale: The implementation cannot be safely automated until maintainers choose whether this is a first-party Control UI surface, a plugin-owned surface, or deferred behind generic plugin UI infrastructure, and how authenticated browser state is scoped and redacted.

options.title: First-party read-only handoff panel
options.body: Add a core/operator-scoped browser panel that initially exposes status, profile, tab context, and resume affordances while gating write actions explicitly.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the browser plugin own the panel after a generic, approved plugin UI entry-point contract lands.

options.title: Defer browser handoff
options.body: Leave users on CLI/agent-mediated manual login until the broader preview and plugin UI security model is settled.

recommendation.title: First-party read-only handoff panel
recommendation.body: Add a core/operator-scoped browser panel that initially exposes status, profile, tab context, and resume affordances while gating write actions explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: They identified the issue as canonical for login handoff and have recent browser/control-UI-adjacent history.
